**I’d pick Starling for budgeting and saving pots.** Its main advantage is that you can *spend directly from a pot* using a free virtual debit card. Monzo also offers virtual cards, but on a paid plan. ([starlingbank.com](https://www.starlingbank.com/features/virtual-cards/?dm_i=4Q2Y%2CQIUT%2C53HT0N%2C39RIC%2C1&utm_source=openai))

Here’s how I’d use Starling’s pots, which it calls **Spaces**:

- **Bills:** Put rent and utilities in a Regular Space and have standing orders and Direct Debits come out of it. That keeps next month’s rent out of the balance you see as available to spend. ([starlingbank.com](https://www.starlingbank.com/features/bills-manager/?utm_source=openai))
- **Groceries:** Give this Space its own virtual card and use it at the till from your phone. The shop comes out of your grocery budget, not your main balance. ([starlingbank.com](https://www.starlingbank.com/features/virtual-cards/?dm_i=4Q2Y%2CQIUT%2C53HT0N%2C39RIC%2C1&utm_source=openai))
- **Holiday or emergency fund:** Use a Space in the **Easy Saver** rather than a Regular Space, so the money earns interest. You can set a target and automate contributions. ([help.starlingbank.com](https://help.starlingbank.com/personal/topics/account-support/what-are-starling-spaces/?utm_source=openai))

**I’d choose Monzo instead if payday is the bit you want to automate.** Its free account’s **Salary Sorter** remembers how you want each pay packet divided between bills, savings and spending. That’s a better fit if you’d rather use one everyday card and just know what’s left to spend. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/salary-sorter?utm_source=openai))
